strategy.chosen: B — pinned upstream LGPL binary distribution
strategy.rejected: A — build FFmpeg from source on the build host
rationale: Same provider, same release branch and the same LGPL configuration as the Windows runtime accepted in AUDIT-005. One licence story, one manifest format, one verification path across both platforms.

Portability. These binaries require at most GLIBC_2.28 (Debian 10 / Ubuntu 18.04 / RHEL 8). A build produced on the current host would hard-require GLIBC_2.39 and the AppImage would refuse to start on anything older — strictly worse than what we ship today.

Self-contained. Every external codec (openh264, kvazaar, svt-av1, dav1d, aom, vpx) is linked statically into the FFmpeg libraries. NEEDED lists only libc/libm/libpthread/libdl/librt/libgcc_s/libmvec and sibling FFmpeg libraries, so there is nothing extra to bundle, hash or keep in sync.

Reproducible by construction: an immutable release tag plus a sha256 over the archive and over every shipped library. A from-source build would have to reproduce a whole cross-toolchain to be equally verifiable.
Maintainable: bumping the version is a manifest edit plus a re-fetch, identical to the Windows flow.
revisit_if: A codec FTHR needs is dropped from the LGPL configuration.
The project needs a glibc baseline older than 2.28, which would require a custom build against an older sysroot.

toolchain.note: Built by the upstream project inside its own container; FTHR does not build it.

glibc.minimum_distribution: anything with glibc >= 2.28 (Debian 10, Ubuntu 18.04, RHEL 8 and newer)

version3_note: --enable-version3 upgrades the licence from LGPLv2.1 to LGPLv3. It does NOT make the build GPL: the binary self-reports 'LGPL version 3 or later'. The same flag is present in the Windows runtime accepted in AUDIT-005, and tools/verify_release_licenses.py deliberately does not treat it as a failure. LGPLv3 is compatible with dynamic linking from non-GPL application code, which is the whole point of the LGPL strategy.

required_capabilities_verified.x11grab: present — the engine's X11 capture backend depends on it

additional_providers_note: Three different FFmpeg builds end up inside the Linux bundle. Only the first is FTHR's choice; the other two arrive inside Python wheels and are used by those wheels alone. All three are LGPL. They are listed so the licence gate can verify them rather than silently accept whatever appears — an FFmpeg library in the artifact is an FFmpeg library being distributed, whether or not anything loads it.

additional_providers.name: Qt Multimedia
additional_providers.origin: official PySide6 6.11.1 Qt runtime (site-packages/PySide6), pinned in requirements-alpha.txt
additional_providers.verified: self-reported banner 'libavcodec license: LGPL version 2.1 or later'; no GPL configure flags
additional_providers.used_by: Qt Multimedia playback only. The FTHR engine never loads these; it needs the .so.62 generation.
additional_providers.note: The equivalent Windows copy (avcodec-61) is documented in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and is conformant for the same reason.

additional_providers.name: OpenCV
additional_providers.origin: opencv-python-headless wheel, pinned to 4.13.0.92 in requirements-alpha.txt. auditwheel renames vendored libraries with an 8-hex-digit hash suffix, e.g. libavcodec-156beeea.so.62.11.100.
additional_providers.verified: no GPL configure flags; banner 'LGPL version 2.1 or later'
additional_providers.note: Same major generation (.so.62) as the pinned runtime but a different build, which is why the hash suffix matters: the loader keeps them apart by SONAME, and the gate keeps them apart by name.

not_hash_pinned_because: The additional providers are artifacts of their wheel versions, not FTHR decisions. Pinning their hashes here would create a second place to update on every PySide6 or OpenCV bump and would drift silently. The wheel pins in requirements-alpha.txt are the control; the licence gate verifies these libraries' licence on every build instead of their bytes.

not_ffmpeg_despite_the_name.libavif: AV1 *image* codec used by Qt and OpenCV. Not FFmpeg. An earlier over-broad cleanup glob ('libav*.so*') deleted it and the bundle then failed at startup with 'ImportError: libavif-...so: cannot open shared object file'.

supersedes.why: Ubuntu 24.04 ships libavcodec.so.60 built with --enable-gpl --enable-libx264 --enable-libx265 --enable-libxvid. Linking the engine against it and bundling the result put the whole AppImage under the GPL, which is what AUDIT-014 recorded.
supersedes.soname_change: The replacement is a different SONAME generation (60->62, 58->60, 7->9, 4->6), so the engine cannot simply be re-pointed at runtime: it must be COMPILED against these headers. That is enforced by FTHR_FFMPEG_ROOT in FTHRcapture_linux/CMakeLists.txt.
